target_customer: Spanish-speaking adults and companies in Latin America who pay for instructor-led online language classes, mainly English
problem: Learning to speak a language in Latin America was taught like a school subject and in-person options were costly or inconvenient. Poliglota offers small live online groups focused on conversation.
business_model: Paid multi-month course plans in USD for individuals plus B2B corporate programs and add-ons

founders.name: Carlos Aravena
founders.background_notes: Named one of El Mercurio's 100 Young Leaders of Chile (2012) per YC page. Education not found.

founders.name: Nicolas Fuenzalida
education: Master's in Organizational Psychology, Universidad Adolfo Ibanez
International University Diploma, Saint Joseph's University
previous_startups: Co-founded four or more companies (per YC page, names not given)

founders.name: Jose Sanchez
previous_startups: Two past startups (per YC page, names not given)
founders.background_notes: Young Leader of Latin America (2015) per YC page. Education not found.

competitors.name: Open English
competitors.what: Online English classes for Latin America and the US Hispanic market
competitors.traction_then: More than 150,000 new students in the first half of 2021 and over 2 million total per a company newswire release
competitors.funding_then: Raised $43M from Insight and Redpoint in an earlier round per TechCrunch

technical_complexity.rationale: Live video classes, scheduling and a teaching method are standard software. The hard part is operations: recruiting and training instructors at scale.

defensibility.rationale: The method and instructor network are copyable and many online language providers exist, though local brand and corporate contracts help.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found and Open English did not absorb the wedge. Poliglota reported breakeven at the end of 2023 per press.

market_need_then: Chilean and Latam professionals needed English for higher income, the company said over 12,000 students had paid about $500, and the pandemic pushed the business from in-person events to online classes per Forbes Chile (2021).

identity.voice_and_tone: Learn by making mistakes, conversation first

branding.brand_signature: The Social Method, which the company says is validated by Harvard (unverified claim)
branding.community_and_virality: Began with language events in bars per an EcosistemaStartup profile and runs conversation clubs; ties with Banchile and Falabella partnerships appear in press.

brand_strength.rationale: Wide Chilean and Latin American business press coverage, partner promotions and a claimed 50,000 students, though the name is a generic Spanish word.

pivots.why: The pandemic forced the move online, per Forbes Chile and La Republica.

outcome_analysis: Poliglota turned a pandemic shock into growth by moving classes online, scaling to about 170 people and reporting breakeven at the end of 2023 after rounds of $2.5M at a stated $50M valuation in 2021. Later money came from small crowdfunding rounds, which suggests no large venture follow-on is visible.
notes: The June 2021 round is from La Tercera as a $2.5M round closed through Y Combinator at a $50M valuation, and Harvard Management Company is named as an investor without an amount. Whether the $50M is post-money is not stated. The 2023 Broota crowdfund was $600K rising to about $700K (Forbes Chile Jan 2023); amount is approximate. A May 2025 round of $1.5M is reported by Emol and Forbes Chile. Press also mentions a prior $2 million round before breakeven in 2023 which may overlap with the 2021 or 2023 rounds, so it is not recorded separately. CB Insights lists a Series A on 2021-05-25 with blank fields and a $4.98M total, unverified. Founding year differs by source (YC 2012, Gust 2010). Open English's TechCrunch $43M raise is an older round.
